newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks fade with miners at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks fade with miners at open.

text.p: The Australian share market continued Monday's retreat at the open on Tuesday as major miners again felt the weight of base metals prices which continued to fall in offshore markets.
From the opening, the All Ordinaries index fell 3.5 points to 2215.7.
Brokers said many investors remained absent from the market, preferring to wait for action on the U.S. interest rate front before commiting themselves to an otherwise lacklustre bourse.
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meets later on Tuesday.
"Plenty of people are still away. They will wait for the meeting in the U.S. tonight," said a Sydney-based dealer.
In the absence of other guidance, base metals prices continued to be the driving force with continued weakness offshore translating to the already hard hit local miners.
"Resources have taken us lower again although there is not a great deal in it so far," said the dealer.
"WMC is getting a hiding, but it is on thin volumes so far."
Turnover wise, CRA was the focus after going ex-dividend on Monday. It accounted for nearly half of early trade by value.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of eight to seven, while about 49 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
